THOUGHT: This 55-year-old retired professional athlete presents with a 10-year history of bilateral wrist and knee pain, morning stiffness lasting ~50 minutes (i.e., prolonged but <60 minutes), absence of systemic inflammation (normal CRP, only mildly elevated ESR), negative rheumatoid factor, and no extra-articular features (e.g., no sicca symptoms, no Raynaud’s, no rash, no uveitis, no nail pitting). Physical exam reveals Heberden’s nodes (non-tender nodules on distal interphalangeal joints — classic for osteoarthritis), tenderness at the base of both thumbs (suggesting first carpometacarpal joint OA), enlarged knees with crepitus and pain on passive ROM, and radiographic findings in both wrists and knees showing joint space narrowing, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and (in knees) subchondral cysts — all hallmark radiographic features of osteoarthritis. While morning stiffness >30 minutes can raise concern for inflammatory arthritis (e.g., RA or PsA), the absence of synovitis (no swelling, no warmth, no systemic inflammation), negative serologies, and dominant involvement of weight-bearing (knees) and commonly overused (wrist/thumb in athletes) joints strongly favors degenerative disease. His athletic history implies repetitive mechanical stress and prior joint trauma — major risk factors for early-onset, polyarticular OA. The pattern is bilateral, symmetrical, and involves DIPs, 1st CMC, wrists, and knees — consistent with generalized osteoarthritis. Rheumatoid arthritis is unlikely given negative RF, normal CRP, lack of erosions or periarticular osteopenia on X-ray, and absence of soft-tissue swelling or deformity. Psoriatic arthritis is less likely without dactylitis, enthesitis, nail changes, or skin findings. Gout or CPPD are possible but unsupported by acute flares, tophi, chondrocalcinosis on imaging, or hyperuricemia. Thus, the totality of clinical, radiographic, and laboratory data points overwhelmingly to primary (degenerative) osteoarthritis — specifically generalized, erosive-appearing in hands (Heberden’s nodes), and advanced in weight-bearing joints.

DIAGNOSIS: Osteoarthritis
